notes: Clean list-plus-claimed-map approach with a defensive copy of the module path. Cross-module override still works at ConfigResource level, and the new unit test locks in dropping the child's non-overridden instance (q).
Owner-map approach with a path-aliasing fix; its unit test enshrines dropping a child import of a different instance, which the reference would honor.
Linear-scan override check fixes the same-module case. It keeps ConfigResource-level cross-module override and is O(n^2); the plan test is solid.
Uses an O(n²) linear scan to keep same-module blocks; the cross-module different-instance override bug remains.
Map-of-slices approach works for the reported case. It still discards child blocks for unrelated instances when any parent block targets the same resource.
Same map-of-slices approach as C3: fixes the issue's scenario but not instance-level parent/child resolution.

Grouping statements per ConfigResource fixes the same-module for_each case. However, a parent block still overrides every child block for that resource, even ones targeting other instances, so those child imports are silently dropped.
Map-of-slices keeps all same-module blocks but still discards every child block once a parent claims the resource; only a basic integration test.
Fixes the reported root-module case. Its unit test explicitly codifies dropping child_c even though the parent never targets it, which is the coarse override the reference fix removes.
Good tests overall, but its fixture explicitly asserts that child's overridden["c"] is dropped, codifying the remaining silent-drop bug.

Moves toward instance-level override by re-parsing static instance keys at config time. It ignores module instance keys and falls back to whole-resource override for dynamic targets, which is fragile and explains the missed hidden test.
Compares static instance keys across modules, a closer approximation, but re-parses addresses in the refactoring package and over-drops whenever keys are dynamic (fails 1 hidden test).
Same claimed-map fix, written with a slice pointer. It retains the coarse parent-over-child override instead of deduplicating per instance after expansion.
Clean fix for the reported root-module case, but keeps per-config-resource cross-module override, which drops child imports of different instances (fails 2 of 3 hidden tests).
Keys the owner map on stringified addresses instead of addrs.Map, which is less idiomatic. Cross-module override remains coarse, and the unit test codifies that behavior.
Works for the reported case but uses string-keyed maps instead of addrs.Map; keeps per-resource override semantics.
Same linear-scan approach as C8. It fixes the reported case but keeps whole-resource cross-module override, which can silently drop child instance imports.
Quadratic scan; fixes only the same-module case and keeps the coarse cross-module override.

Removes config-level dedup and emits child statements before parent ones, so the later knownImports.Put gives parent precedence per instance. This matches the reference semantics, though it relies implicitly on overwrite order rather than an explicit check, and the test covers only the root for_each case.

Removes config-level dedup and visits children before parents so the parent's block wins per instance via map overwrite; simple and matches reference semantics, though it relies on implicit last-write-wins and adds only a basic test.
Tidy owner-map implementation that fixes the root for_each case. It shares the coarse cross-module override flaw.
Clean owner-map fix for same-module blocks; still drops child blocks for other instances when a parent targets the same resource.
Clean owner-map fix with a plan test covering multiple blocks in both root and child modules. It does not handle instance-level parent/child override.
Owner-map fix with a test covering for_each imports in both root and child, but no handling of parent and child targeting different instances.
Essentially the same claimed-map approach as C2/C13 with a slice pointer. It shares the coarse cross-module override flaw, and the package suite failed.
Logic is equivalent to the other owner-map variants, but the package suite failed and the cross-module instance-level case is unresolved.
Owner-map approach keeps all same-module blocks. Cross-module override remains ConfigResource-granular, so a parent block for one instance discards child blocks for other instances.
Fixes same-module for_each imports, but still overrides at the ConfigResource level, so a parent block silently drops child blocks that target other instances; good unit and integration tests.
Correct and complete, but adds unnecessary parser wrapper methods at the end of parse.go and mixes calling styles; tests mostly check only no-error and segment count.
Fix is complete, but it adds a redundant layer of parser wrapper methods on top of the Token helpers; tests mostly only check that there is no error and the segment count.

Misses the nested branch of NextBlock (`d.Val() == "}"/"{" && !d.nextOnSameLine()`), so quoted braces still change nesting during NextSegment and break nested blocks inside route/handle; only the issue's simple example is fixed.

Misses the NextBlock inner nesting loop, so a quoted brace at end of line still changes nesting when tokens are walked via NextBlock (e.g. NextSegment in nested matchers or route); its tests don't exercise this.
Correct, using Dispenser helpers plus inline checks in addresses and doImport; its three test cases are minimal and omit a quoted "}" inside a site block.
Covers all brace checks, including the NextBlock inner loop, but mixes Dispenser helpers with inline Quoted() checks; it adds only three thin table test cases.
Correct at every site, but the `&& !Token().Quoted()` check is repeated inline instead of factored into a helper; tests are only a few table cases.
Correct and complete, but repeats inline `Val()==... && !Quoted()` checks everywhere instead of a helper; tests are basic table cases.
Complete fix with Token and Dispenser helpers (redundant wasQuoted check left in directive()); thorough tests include unbalanced-brace errors, a snippet case, and an adapt fixture.
Complete fix with Token and bounds-checked Dispenser helpers, though it keeps the redundant wasQuoted check; strong tests include unbalanced-brace errors, snippets and an adapt test.
Adds Token helpers and uses them at every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser; it leaves a now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive() and has solid dispenser and parse tests.

Updates every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser with clean Token helpers; it keeps a now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive(), and its tests cover args, nested blocks and snippets.
Clean and complete, mirroring the reference structure; strong tests cover segments, an unbalanced-brace error case, snippets with block placeholders, and an adapt fixture.

Essentially matches the reference (minus the minor quoted '{}' and HasSuffix tweaks), drops the redundant check, and has thorough tests including an unbalanced-brace error case, import blocks and an adapt test.

Complete fix, though addresses() uses an inline check while everything else uses the helper; the dispenser test exercises NextBlock directly on quoted braces, and the live-server integration test is a bit heavy.
Complete fix with one inline check in addresses; its dispenser test iterates NextBlock without consuming args (exercising the inner nesting loop), and it adds an integration test.
Complete, idiomatic helper-based fix; tests are limited to table entries in TestParseOneAndImport.
Complete fix equivalent to the reference; tests are only table cases checking segment lengths.
Same code as C1 and complete; tests are only table cases in TestParseOneAndImport.
Clean, reference-equivalent implementation with Token helpers; table tests cover open/close braces and a nested block followed by a quoted brace.
Complete fix with Token helpers and atOpenBrace/atCloseBrace Dispenser wrappers; good dispenser test plus parse table cases.
Complete and clean, with Token helpers plus bounds-safe at*Brace dispenser wrappers and the redundant check removed; dispenser and parser tests are good.
Complete fix; its dispenser test covers a quoted "}" alone on a line inside a block, which directly exercises NextBlock nesting.
Complete, clean fix; a dispenser test walks NextBlock token-by-token with standalone quoted braces, validating the inner nesting logic.
Complete fix with Token helpers plus bounds-checked Dispenser wrappers (slightly redundant, since Token() already bounds-checks); tests verify segment contents and the snippet path.
Complete, consistent use of helpers across dispenser and parser; tests check segment contents, backtick quoting and snippet import.
Correct, but helpers and inline wasQuoted checks are mixed inconsistently and the redundant check is kept; decent dispenser and parse tests.
Correct and complete, but helpers live only on Dispenser so the doImport switch and addresses use inline wasQuoted checks; tests are decent.
Looks up branch pages via treePages.Get and only applies slugs when the page's dir equals the section base, missing nested directories; breaks the package suite.

Queries the raw treePages per prefix and only rewrites a regular page's dir when it equals the section base, so pages in nested non-section dirs keep the old path; the change also breaks the package suite.

Prefix-map replacement works, but adds two descriptor fields, an always-nil error return and a pageState type assertion, and relies on ToLower matching, which is fragile for normalized names when DisablePathToLower is set.
Prefix-matching slug replacement works, but it adds two separate descriptor fields and an error return that is always nil, and the test does not cover nested non-section dirs.
Correct prefix-map approach with separate SectionBase/ContainerDir overrides; ToLower-based matching against Path() is slightly fragile for unnormalized paths.
Prefix-matched replacement is correct for the common cases and skips standalone and home pages, but it allocates a map per page and lowercases to match rather than reusing the unnormalized base.
Works by building a full path and injecting it as ExpandedPermalink, which conflates slugs with permalink config; the prefix-map logic itself handles gaps and unnormalized paths.
Prefix-matched slug replacement is correct, including gap sections and unnormalized paths, but it overloads ExpandedPermalink to carry a non-permalink path.

Builds the slugged path from the branch chain (handling gaps and nested dirs) and feeds it through the permalink branch; that exposes it to QueryUnescape (e.g. '+' becomes a space) and reuses permalink semantics somewhat hackily.
Piggybacks on the permalink path (QueryUnescape, Clean, ExpandedPermalink), which is hacky, and a slugged gap section replaces the whole relative path, dropping intermediate dirs.
Replaces a regular page's whole container dir with the slugged section path, flattening nested non-section directories (wrong URLs, possible collisions); fails a hidden test.

Replaces a regular page's whole container dir with the current section's slugged path, so pages in non-section subdirs collapse into the section (risking collisions), and a slugged gap section loses its intermediate dirs.

Passes a section-path to slug map in the descriptor and applies it by prefix in CreateTargetPaths; correct including gaps and DisablePathToLower, though the map-in-descriptor design is slightly heavier.

Passes a map of slugs keyed by consistently normalized or unnormalized section path into the descriptor and applies it in CreateTargetPaths; this is correct, though putting a map in the descriptor is a bit heavy.
Compact section-chain map with a prefix walk and a single SlugDir override; correct in normal cases, with minor fragility from lowercase matching when DisablePathToLower is set.

Collects the slugs from the section chain and replaces dir segments by matching path prefixes, which handles nested non-section dirs and gap sections; it lowercases to match instead of reusing the unnormalized base, so a DisablePathToLower path with spaces could slip through.

Replaces section path elements by depth using SectionsEntries, which handles gap sections, nested non-section directories, unnormalized paths and ugly URLs; tests cover all of these plus taxonomy and term pages.
Indexes by SectionsEntries depth, restricts the change to relevant kinds and pages without a url override, and has strong tests covering gap sections, ugly URLs and taxonomies/terms.
Same map-in-descriptor approach as C5 and correct, but uses an unchecked sp.(*pageState) assertion where sp.Slug() would suffice.
Uses a slug map in the descriptor much like C6 and is correct, but relies on an unchecked *pageState type assertion on ancestors.

Clean depth-indexed replacement while walking the CurrentSection/Parent chain, with a single Dir override via cmp.Or; correct for nested sections, gaps, non-section subdirectories and taxonomies, and tested accordingly.
Replaces dir elements by index derived from each slugged section's depth, which is robust to case, normalization and gap sections, and its tests cover deep non-section dirs and bundles.
Essentially the same sound depth-based approach as C2 over Ancestors, with good tests; also edits user docs, which is relevant but beyond what was needed.
Uses the same depth-indexed replacement as C3, which is correct for gaps and plain dirs, and also updates the docs; the docs change is relevant but goes beyond the task.
Rebuilds the path from BaseNameNoIdentifier of each section, so intermediate directories are lost when a nested section's parent section is not its immediate directory (gap sections).
Rebuilds the section path from each section's BaseNameNoIdentifier, so it drops intermediate non-section dirs, e.g. help/sub/deep becomes /ayuda/deep, whenever any ancestor has a slug.
Deliberately skips slug application for regular pages not directly in their section's directory, so pages in nested subdirectories keep the untranslated section name; fails a hidden test.
Ignores section slugs entirely for pages whose container dir is not the section itself, leaving such pages at /help/... while the section moves to /ayuda.
Passes hidden tests, but `GetExec() != ""` always marks exec as explicitly "default", there are no run-level integration tests, and the package suite fails.

A clean internal/cmd implementation applied after consolidation that passes the hidden tests. It does not drop env/config-layer shortcuts before the merge or reject execution-segment flags, always sets exec to 'default', and the package suite fails.
Odd placement (helper appended after syncWriter, a CLI error constructor in lib/executor), exec is always set explicitly, tests are thinner, and hidden tests fail 0/5.

The logic is functionally right, but it leaks a CLI-specific OnceConflictError helper into lib/executor and always materializes exec='default'. It misses lower-layer shortcut handling, and its tests (TestRunOnce plus a generic `logs` helper) fail with the hidden suite.

The post-consolidation ApplyOnce in lib/executor is correct, the exec null-ness is preserved, and the flag is registered on run, archive and cloud run, but hidden tests fail 0/5 (most likely because the added TestRunOnce name collides), and lower-layer shortcut handling and execution-segment rejection are missing.

The code is reasonable, with a good exec null handling and wiring for run/archive/cloud run. However, it appends TestRunOnce to cmd_run_test.go, which likely collides with the hidden tests (0/5), and lower-layer shortcuts are not handled.
Clean, minimal implementation, but tests are modest (no env/setup/archive checks) and hidden tests fail 0/5 (TestRunOnce collision).

The post-consolidation ApplyOnce works, but it puts CLI-specific '--once' errors in the public lib/executor package. It misses lower-layer shortcut (env/config) wiping and execution-segment conflicts, and its TestRunOnce likely collides with the hidden tests, giving 0/5.

Works and passes hidden tests, but conflict validation lives in loadAndConfigureLocalTest while the transform lives in consolidate, so paths that bypass the former skip the check; the package suite fails and lower-layer shortcuts are not handled.

It works for the hidden tests, but conflict validation is split into loadAndConfigureLocalTest, away from where the flag is applied. Some tests assert exact info-log sequences (fragile), and the package suite fails.

Self-contained once.go with a good error listing scenario names and thorough tests, but conflict detection goes indirectly through cliConfig validity, BaseConfig is rebuilt with a string-literal type, and hidden tests fail 0/5.

A well-structured onceFlagSet is wired into run/archive/cloud, conflict detection uses CLI options, and the error lists sorted scenario names. Tests are thorough, but the TestRunOnce name collision fails the hidden suite, and lower-layer shortcut wiping is still unhandled.

Clean getOnce plus ApplyOnce applied after consolidation, with thorough integration, archive and unit tests, but hidden tests fail 0/5 (likely a TestRunOnce name collision) and lower-layer shortcuts and execution-segment are not handled.

A solid implementation with conflict checks moved before the CLI getter and good unit and archive tests. The TestRunOnce name collision fails the hidden suite, and it shares the same env/config-layer gap as the others.

Solid applyOnceFlag wrapper over executor.ApplyOnce, registered on run, archive and cloud run, with thorough tests and all suites passing; the countOccurrences helper needlessly reimplements strings.Count.

A correct flag set is wired into run/archive/cloud run, and the ApplyOnce transform passes both suites, with good archive and integration tests. The countOccurrences helper needlessly reimplements strings.Count, and env/config shortcut wiping is unhandled.

Well-organized internal/cmd/once.go with the flag registered on run, archive and cloud, comprehensive tests including archive metadata, and all suites passing; it shares the missing env/config shortcut handling.

A clean internal/cmd implementation with separate request/validate/apply helpers that passes both suites. Tests are comprehensive, including -i shorthand and archive checks. It misses lower-layer shortcut dropping and execution-segment conflicts.

Closest in structure to the reference (internal/cmd/once.go, sorted scenario names in the error, help example), with strong unit, integration and archive tests and all suites passing; it lacks only the lower-layer shortcut dropping and execution-segment rejection.

A cohesive applyOnceFlag on a dedicated flag set for run/archive/cloud gives sorted scenario names in errors and passes both suites. Unit, integration and archive-metadata tests are strong. It still lacks lower-layer shortcut dropping.

Minimal and clean: the flag is in optionFlagSet and ApplyOnce runs after consolidation, passing hidden tests, but it has no archive or setup/teardown test, the package suite fails, and it shares the missing env/config-shortcut edge case.
Essentially the same sound approach as C5 and it passes the hidden tests. The sumIterations helper duplicates the existing sum, the package suite fails, and lower-layer shortcut handling is missing.

Clean: the flag is validated before consolidation and ApplyOnce applied after it, with exit codes, good integration tests checking tags/env/setup/teardown, and all suites passing; it has no archive test and adds public API to lib/executor.

Simple, correct post-consolidation transform with conflict checks before the merge, and both suites pass. Integration tests cover setup/teardown, exec/env/tags, multiple scenarios and every conflicting flag. It misses env/config-layer shortcut dropping and execution-segment conflicts, and puts the CLI error in lib/executor.
Logic is scattered across config.go and options.go, exec is always made explicit via `!= ""`, BaseConfig is overwritten manually, and hidden tests fail 0/5 despite decent tests including archive.

It functions correctly, but always sets exec='default' and uses a roundabout BaseConfig replacement. The once logic is spread across config.go and options.go, and the TestRunOnce collision causes hidden test failure.
The behavior is functionally equivalent to the others, but it introduces a redundant OnceScenarioError type in the public executor package, and hidden tests fail 0/5 (TestRunOnce collision).

It introduces an unnecessary new exported OnceScenarioError type in lib/executor, and isOnceSet swallows flag errors. The transform is otherwise correct, but the TestRunOnce added to cmd_run_test.go breaks the hidden suite.
Correct wrapping approach, but changes applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr's signature with a clunky parenPos parameter (callers pass 0 as a sentinel), and omits the Pretty unary-plus fix.
Correct and uses accurate paren positions, but adds a parenPos parameter to applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr that is a dummy 0 at the non-wrapped call site.
Minimal, correct wrapping in both paths via a recursive applyUnaryOp call; it has a redundant range check and lacks the Pretty fix.
A minimal fix that matches the reference design (wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr in the paren rule and in applyUnary); it leaves Pretty unfixed and gives the inner node a slightly off StartPos.

Wraps plain literals as a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr in both the paren and unary-paren paths, and includes the same Pretty fix as the reference; its added positivity check catches `(0)` but not `-(5)`.
Close to the reference, including the Pretty unary-plus fix, and adds a parse-time `(0)` range check with a test; `-(5)` in a range is not caught at parse time.
Correct wrapping, with a recursive constant check preserving positivity and div/mod errors, but no tests exercise those added validations.
Correct wrap plus preserved zero, division and modulo checks, but it adds no tests for the changed validation paths.

Adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral, changes its String(), and adds asDurationExpr conversions in several grammar rules, producing a mixed representation that is more invasive and fragile than needed.

Works by adding a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral, changing NumberLiteral.String, and inserting asDurationExpr shims in several grammar rules; this is invasive and creates two parenthesis mechanisms, though it keeps the parse-time zero checks.
Nearly identical to the reference with one clean helper used in both paths, plus an end-to-end durationVisitor test; only the Pretty unary-plus tweak is missing.
Nearly mirrors the reference structure with a unified wrapDurationExpr helper, and adds a durationVisitor evaluation test; it lacks the Pretty tweak.

Includes the Pretty fix, positivity checks, and strong tests (AST, error, and end-to-end), but paren_duration_expr uses an unconditional `.(*NumberLiteral)` assertion that would panic on any future non-literal node.
Includes the Pretty fix, a positive-duration check and excellent tests (AST, errors, visitor eval), but the paren rule does an unchecked $2.(*NumberLiteral) assertion, which is fragile.

Works, but sets Range/OriginalOffset and RangeExpr/OriginalOffsetExpr at the same time, reorders printer logic to cope, rewrites the matrix/subquery actions, and adds a new experimental-flag check: substantial scope creep with a new dual-field invariant.

Fixes the round-trip but adds eager constant resolution in addOffsetExpr and the matrix/subquery rules, reorders the subquery step printer, and adds a new experimental-flag check on `-(5)`; this is broad, unnecessary scope.
Minimal and correct wrapping in both paths, close to the reference; it uses the literal's position rather than the paren's and lacks the Pretty fix.
A small, clean wrap helper used in both paren paths; it has no Pretty fix and no zero-check preservation, and the StartPos points at the literal rather than the paren.

The AST-field approach (NumberLiteral.Wrapped plus a String() change) works and conveniently keeps div-by-zero checks, but it changes the public AST and needs special-casing in offset_expr and positive_duration_expr.
Adds a public NumberLiteral.Wrapped field and converts the literal at the offset and range consumers; it works, but it is a more invasive AST/printer change with scattered special-casing.
Correct wrapping, and a recursive constant-value helper keeps parse-time positivity and div/mod-by-zero errors; this goes beyond the issue but is well tested with error cases and eval tests.
A correct fix that preserves zero, division and modulo parse checks, with error and promqltest eval tests; the DurationExpr construction is inlined in two places and Pretty is not addressed.
Wraps literals at the grammar level in both paths, preserves positivity errors for `(0)` and `-(5)` with tests, and adds eval tests; the Pretty fix is missing.
A clean wrap approach that keeps the positive-duration parse errors for `(0)` and `-(5)`, with strong tests including promqltest evaluation cases.
Correct, with thorough validation and tests, but changes applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr to take an awkward *Item parameter and leaves an unrelated change to the generated-file header comment.

Thorough handling of zero, division and range checks via a recursive constant helper, but it changes the signature to an *Item pointer and leaves an unrelated goyacc header change from regenerating in another directory.
Clean wrap helper applied in both grammar paths, with a recursive positivity check; no tests cover the new positivity validation, and the Pretty fix is missing.
Wraps the literal in both paren paths and preserves the positive-duration parse check; it changes that check without adding a test for it and leaves the div/mod zero checks bypassable.

The ReturnError travels inside ExecError rather than as its own panic, so try swallows it. A bare return in a partial yields nil instead of the rendered output. The `return A | B` to `A | B | return` rewrite is a hacky divergence, built on a dummy 'x' func parse.

Routes return through the ExecError path, so `try` swallows it; a bare return in a partial yields nil; and the new normalizeReturn pipeline rewriting adds the kind of transform complexity the issue wanted removed.

This is the least intrusive approach: a wrapped-error sentinel with no exec.go changes, and its bare and valued semantics match the reference. Because walkTemplate never traps, a return inside a block or define kills the outer page. try also swallows return, and node.go in the fork is edited.

Avoids touching the executor and relies on wrapped error propagation, so `try` swallows a return and a return inside a `template`-invoked template terminates the whole outer template; bare-return output semantics are correct.

Semantics are correct for bare and valued partial returns, try and template calls, with excellent unit and integration tests. It extends the Executer interface and changes the executeWithState signature, which is more intrusive to the fork than needed.

Clean executor-level trap that returns the ReturnError through a new Executer method, with correct bare-return and `try` handling and a good executor unit test; the interface change is a bit invasive, and it lacks the pipeline-position check.
walkTemplate has no trap, so a bare return in a block or define ends the outer template. HasReturn discards partial output and makes a bare return yield nil. Arg grouping is limited to partials.
No walkTemplate trap, so returns from `define`d templates escape to the caller; it keeps HasReturn with output discarding, a bare return gives nil, and argument wrapping is limited to partials.
Solid and close to C1, with args grouping and a too-many-args error. It omits the try re-panic, so try swallows return, and it swallows valued returns in template calls.
Correct HasValue and walkTemplate trapping with good tests, but it does not stop `try` from swallowing the return sentinel.

A recoverReturn helper is used at both template and walkTemplate boundaries, and try is handled. Keeping HasReturn, with save/restore for sub-templates, means partials containing return lose their output, and a bare return yields nil.
Good trapping and `try` handling, but it keeps HasReturn so partials with any return discard output, and both a bare return and a fall-through yield nil.

Clean implementation matching the reference on bare-return output, try re-panic and block/template trapping. Tests are solid, including the baseof footer and try cases. There is no arg-count validation, valued returns in sub-templates are swallowed, and docs churn is added.

Correct design covering HasValue, the `template` trap, `try` propagation and argument grouping, with thorough tests; it moves `return` to the templates namespace, contains a slightly misleading doc line, and lacks the last-in-pipeline check.

A sentinel error is panicked from evalCall and trapped in errRecover and walkTemplate. A bare return keeps the partial's rendered output, try re-panics the sentinel, `return add . 42` is grouped, and too many args errors. However, walkTemplate also swallows valued returns from sub-templates, unlike the reference, and the misuse errors are missing.

Correct overall with HasValue semantics, `template` trapping, `try` propagation and argument grouping; it moves `return` to the templates namespace, which is unnecessary but harmless, and does not enforce the last-in-pipeline rule.
The executor trapping is reasonable and try is handled. Dropping argument grouping breaks `return add . 42`, and a bare return in a partial returns nil instead of the output.
Trapping and `try` handling are fine, but dropping the argument wrapping breaks `return add . 42`, and a bare return in a partial returns nil instead of the rendered output.
There is no argument grouping, so the existing `{{ return add . 42 }}` form breaks, which is a backward-compat regression. try swallows return, and a bare return in a partial yields nil.
Never wraps `return add . 42`, which breaks existing behavior; it also lets `try` swallow return, and a bare return or fall-through in a partial returns nil.

walkTemplate has no trap, so a return in a block or define aborts the whole page. A bare return yields nil. The `return x | y` pipeline-wrapping semantics diverge from the reference, and the test was rewritten to expect success.
Missing the `template` trap and the bare-return output semantics; it also redefines `return A | B` to wrap the whole pipeline and rewrites the existing issue test to match that choice.

The core mechanism and bare-return semantics match the reference, with good hugolib coverage. try is not taught to re-raise return, so `try (return x)` swallows it. Valued returns in sub-templates are swallowed, and the docs edits widen scope.

Solid sentinel-panic design: values are returned, a bare return yields the rendered output, returns inside `template` calls are trapped, and `return fn args` is still supported; however `try` swallows a return and a return that is not last in a pipeline is not detected.
walkTemplate has no trap, so a return inside a block or define (e.g. baseof main) kills the whole page. A bare return in a partial yields nil, and there is no arg-count check.
No trap in walkTemplate, so a return inside a `template` call aborts the whole outer template, and a bare return yields nil; the basic early return with a value works.

Keeps HasReturn and discards output for any partial containing return. A bare or unreached return therefore yields nil instead of the rendered output, deviating from the reference. try and template-call trapping are handled.

Keeps HasReturn, so any partial containing return discards its output, and both a bare return and a fall-through give nil instead of the rendered output; it does trap returns in `template` calls and handles `try`.
